newsitem.title: USA: Southmark gets $3.9 mln fund settlement.
newsitem.headline: Southmark gets $3.9 mln fund settlement.

text.p: Southmark Corp said on Wednesday it received a $3.9 million payment from the Milken Global Settlement Fund, for settlement of claims it filed against Michael Milken and certain of his affiliates.

The company said this was an interim payment and it might receive a final distribution from the fund in 1997. Southmark said it received $26.5 million from the fund as an initial payment in February 1995.
Southmark said it was one of many companies which bought and issued so-called junk bonds through financier Milken, who pioneered the instrument.
Milken later pleaded guilty to six securities-related crimes in 1990 then served two years in prison and paid more than $1 billion in fines.

Milken's $1.3 million global settlement fund, to settle company claims, was funded by Milken, certain of his affiliates and other settling participants, certain insurance proceeds and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Milken Civil Disgorgement Fund, Southmark said.
The company said any further distribution would require court approval.
